name: Shelob baseline
description: The initial Software Factory requirements. Numeric thresholds are configurable advisory starting points, not universal limits.

rules.title: Change size
rules.rationale: Large changes take more work to review. Consider splitting work that can stand alone. Size alone does not make a change wrong.

rules.title: Changed areas
rules.rationale: Explain why the changed areas belong together. A directory count cannot tell us whether the work is related.

rules.title: Change scope and dependencies
rules.rationale: Check for unrelated work or dependencies on another change. Related tests, generated files, and required migrations can belong in the same PR.
rules.instructions: Trace what the change does and what it depends on. Report unrelated work only when the edits have separate purposes and the code supports that claim. Suggest a split only if each part can be reviewed and applied on its own. Leave uncertain boundaries unresolved.

rules.title: Skipped or focused tests
rules.rationale: New skip or focus markers can keep tests out of a normal run. Check whether that is intentional. Ignore markers in strings and comments.

rules.title: Assertion count
rules.rationale: Check what the removed assertions covered. Helpers and equivalent rewrites may preserve the same coverage. An assertion count cannot prove that a test is weaker.

rules.title: Tests for changed behavior
rules.rationale: Tests should check behavior against an independently chosen expected result. Existing tests may cover the change. Reversible edits with little impact may not need new tests.
rules.instructions: Read the code and related tests. Look for tests that mock the unit under test, copy expected values from the implementation, swallow failures, or omit await. Check whether tests cover important changed branches. Name the behavior and a specific incorrect implementation the tests would miss. Do not report weaker tests just because assertion counts fell or test files did not change. Never invent a test result.

rules.title: Test and CI settings
rules.rationale: Ignored failures and lower coverage limits can hide regressions. Read the changed setting and check why it changed.

rules.title: PR description
rules.rationale: The PR description should say what changed, why, and which checks ran. A missing description stays unchecked.
rules.instructions: Compare the description with the change. Point out important omissions and unsupported claims. Do not require a template or specific headings. Separate planned checks from checks that ran.

rules.title: Visual evidence
rules.rationale: Screenshots, recordings, or a working preview can help reviewers check visible changes. A UI file change alone does not require them.
rules.instructions: Check whether the change affects appearance or interaction. Suggest a view or state only if it helps verify the change. Do not require screenshots for logic changes in UI files or refactors with no visual effect. Missing attachments stay unknown unless the user supplied the evidence set.
